excerpt: const [moveError] = overwrite ? await settle(rename(temp, output)) : await settle(link(temp, output));
sink: writes remote asset bytes to an attacker-chosen absolute local path via fs rename/link
guard: bypassable: overwrite is set by the same caller, so the no-clobber default is not an independent guard; there is no path allow-list at all
why: path is resolved with resolve() at line 455 with no jail/allow-list, then asset content fetched from the Editor is written to that exact path (temp file, then rename/link at line 556, verified against source). A caller can target files like ~/.bashrc or ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, and the content written originates from a project asset that could itself be attacker-influenced via store_download/sketchfab_import or a malicious collaborator with edit access.
contract: Download an asset to a local file. Downloads are limited to 512 MiB and never overwrite unless overwrite=true.

sink: reads any file the Node process's OS user can read (via node:fs readFile/open+read) and uploads its bytes into the project as a new/replacement asset
why: asset.path is caller-controlled with no project-root jail or allow-list; resolve() only normalizes it, then the upload() helper (lines 93-169) reads the file with readFile or open+read and base64-encodes it to the Editor via wss.raw('assets:upload'/'files:upload:*'). An agent tricked into passing an absolute path like ~/.ssh/id_rsa exfiltrates its contents into the PlayCanvas project, which may later be visible to other collaborators or published in a build.

param: none (IPAPI_API_TOKEN is operator configuration, not a caller-supplied argument)
sink: writes the full outbound request URL (with the API token embedded as a ?key= query parameter, see src/utils/transport.util.ts fetchIpApi) plus the raw JSON response body to a file under /tmp/mcp/<project-name>/, created via recursive mkdirSync and written with fs.writeFileSync's default (world-readable) mode
why: fetchIpApi unconditionally appends key=<IPAPI_API_TOKEN> to the request URL whenever a token is configured (regardless of includeExtendedData), and that exact URL string is passed straight into saveRawResponse -> buildResponseContent -> fs.writeFileSync with no redaction. On a shared/multi-user host, any other local user can list /tmp/mcp/<project>/ and read the token out of the plaintext log file. This fires automatically on every call when a token is configured -- no malicious argument is needed -- which is why it is Tier B (config-dependent) rather than Tier A (no caller-controlled argument drives the leak).

param: none (IPAPI_API_TOKEN is operator configuration, not a caller-supplied argument)
sink: same underlying sink as ip_get_details: src/tools/ipaddress-link.tool.ts calls the identical ipAddressController.get, which goes through fetchIpApi -> saveRawResponse -> fs.writeFileSync
why: ip_get_details_link shares ipAddressController.get with ip_get_details verbatim (confirmed by reading both tool files), so the same unconditional token-in-URL-then-written-to-/tmp behavior applies here too; the only addition in this tool is an inert 'ip://<resolvedIp>' resource_link string in the response, which does not affect this finding.
contract: Uses the same arguments and output rendering pipeline as ip_get_details.

why: The compiled entrypoint is src/index.ts per tsconfig (rootDir/include src/**/*); topic is only interpolated into plain-text Google search query strings typed into a headless-browser search box (src/deep-research.ts), and subsequent URLs visited come from Google's own extracted result links, not from topic directly; no path/command/eval sink is reachable from the caller-controlled argument, and grepping the whole src tree found no exec/spawn/eval/new Function anywhere in this repo.

Each query is typed into Google's own search box via Puppeteer (no shell/URL built from the raw string); the only local filesystem write (src/parallel-search.ts saveResults) builds its filename via query.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '_'), which strips every character outside [a-z0-9] including '/', '\\' and '.', so path traversal via the query argument is not possible, and outputDir is not exposed in the tool's inputSchema in src/index.ts at all (only 'queries' and 'maxParallel' are) -- it is fixed to a server-side default under os.tmpdir().

sink: page.goto(url) drives a real headless Chromium instance (Puppeteer) to the caller-supplied URL and the tool returns the extracted page content back to the caller
guard: partial: isValidUrl only restricts the URL scheme to http/https (blocking file:// etc.), but does not block loopback/RFC1918/link-local/cloud-metadata hosts such as http://169.254.169.254/ or http://localhost:<port>/
why: visit_page's stated purpose is fetch-the-URL-you-give-me, which the task's own anti-false-positive rule caps at Tier B absent a further twist; the twist here is that it is a full browser rather than a simple HTTP client, with zero host-based restriction, so a caller (or an agent steered by page content it already visited) can direct it at internal network services or cloud metadata endpoints and get the rendered page text back through extractContentAsMarkdown.
contract: Visit a webpage and extract its content
